question: Can the P0571B baryon-only activation calculate an apparent-gravity arrival map that predicts normalized cluster lens morphology without using the target map?

formula.conservation: B_100 and every arrival map are nonnegative and separately unit normalized inside 250 kpc; f only redistributes normalized response.
formula.parameters: one universal routed fraction f plus one universal arrival smoothing width; no cluster-specific parameter

validation.selection: Choose one carrier, width, and fraction by minimum equal-system mean Lenstool-ensemble Jensen-Shannon divergence on development systems only.
validation.holdout: Score the single locked candidate on the three different systems.
validation.method_control: Score the locked candidate and local control against GLAFIC best maps without reselection.
validation.uncertainty: Score both against all 100 Lenstool realizations per system.
validation.spent_disclosure: All ten systems are globally spent and the split was previously used by P0568; P0572 is prospective only to this activation formula.

advance_gates.raw_lensing_followup: Authorize a separately frozen raw-image-position test only if every gate passes.

cross_domain.galaxy: The activation is zero for net axisymmetric baryonic component fields, so this layer changes no SPARC rotation speed and cannot replace the required radial scalar law.
cross_domain.solar: The activation is exactly zero for one centered source, giving zero Solar force and zero Mercury change.
cross_domain.scope: P0572 tests a possible angular destination law, not absolute lensing strength or galaxy dynamics.

claim_limits: The targets are normalized standard-GR convergence reconstructions, not raw lensing observables or absolute mass.
The source map contains photometric member light but omits gas, ICL, and mass-to-light variation.
The carrier and smoothing choices translate an empirical location invariant into a destination law; they are not derived from an action.
The development/holdout systems are globally spent, and P0571B was motivated by their prior peak analysis.
A successful normalized map does not establish correct image multiplicity, shear, time delays, or gravity strength.
